Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Show love and kindness to others, following the teachings of Jesus
Situation2: They notice someone in their circle going through difficulties and respond with care
Story: It was 2 a.m. when my phone buzzed, jolting me awake. My best friend’s name flashed on the screen, and I answered to the sound of her sobbing. She could barely get the words out—her father had just been rushed to the hospital. As her friend, I knew I needed to listen, to be present, to let her pour out her pain. But as she spoke, I remembered that just yesterday, I’d promised to check in on a woman from church who was struggling alone after surgery. I’d planned to bring her groceries and pray with her in the morning. Now, I felt torn. My friend needed me, maybe all night, but so did this woman who had no one else. I wanted to be the friend who stayed on the line, but also the Christian who showed up with love and kindness. The weight of both expectations pressed on me, and I lay there, phone in hand, heart racing, unsure which need I should answer first.
